chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said:
The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: 'Whoever has intercourse with a woman once, and then she is taken (by her guardian/father), she has no option (of khiyar al-ruju').'

key_terms.خِيَار: Option/Right to choose (specifically khiyar al-ruju' in marriage context)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a woman's right to choose (khiyar) if her guardian takes her back after marriage?
ai.summary: This ruling from Imam Ali (peace be upon him) clarifies that the right of option (khiyar al-ruju') is contingent upon the woman's physical presence in the husband's home; once she is 'taken' (consummated or fully transferred), the option is extinguished. This distinction highlights the Shia juristic emphasis on the actualization of marital rights through physical union as the threshold for finalizing the contract's irrevocability.
